text.p: French drinks group Remy-Cointreau reported a sharp drop in 1996/97 first-half profit on Tuesday after recording a drop in exceptional gains related to debt restructuring.

Remy, best known for its Remy Martin cognacs, Krug and Piper-Heidsieck champagnes and Mount Gay rum, said pre-tax attributable income for the six months to September 30 fell to 41 million francs ($7.8 million) from 215 million in the year-earlier period.

Its pre-tax, pre-exceptional loss shrank to one million francs from 39 million francs, and Remy said it expected the improving trend to be helped by a "satisfying" level of activity seen at the start of the second half begun in October.
Turnover rose four percent to 3.07 billion francs in the first half on a three percent increase in volumes sold, it said in a statement.
Operating profit fell to 210 million francs from 216 million in the year-earlier period. The decline partly reflected a 60 million franc rise in promotional expenses to develop Remy-Cointreau brands.
Remy's financial expense narrowed to 211 million francs from 255 million, helped by a reduction in debt, which stood at 6.6 billion francs a year ago.

It recorded an exceptional gain of 44 million francs in the first half, down from 257 million a year earlier. It said the exceptional gains were due essentially to the restructuring of part of the debt.
Remy did not disclose the debt level at the end of the 1996/97 first half in its statement.
